selections.comment: BETA READER arrives in decent form having gone well in a first time visor (retained) to be placed over a mile last time and can take another step forward to land this. A winner on Tapeta last term at Wolverhampton the drop back to 7f here looks ideal and he looks the most solid option. Due Respect is feared most having knocked loudly on the door the last twice (both at Redcar over 7f on fast ground). The surface is a potential issue as she went very poorly on it at Wolverhampton but did run close to par at Southwell, even if only 8th of 10. Ey Up He's A Star is a danger having placed on handicap debut last time and on only his fifth start a little further improvement is likely but Marsh Meadow is the potential fly in the ointment having been given a potentially lenient opening mark for this handicap debut on the balance of her three runs in novice/maiden company. Seven furlongs looks to suit and if at ease on the surface she could play a big role

If taking to this Tapeta surface she'll go very close to adding a sixth career win from just 10 runs. However, she may find WADACRE GOMEZ a tad too strong if Charlie Johnston's charge is on song. A bit hit or miss, he hit form again last time and off 2lb lower than his last winning mark he can add to his seven career wins. Fantasy Believer and Royal Approval hold claims on the pick of their form but Penzance could offer fair each way value returned to the AW after a poor spell on turf. He's much more reliable on an artificail surface and is back on his last winning mark in March and can reach the frame

selections.comment: The hugely promising Boiling Point makes his handicap debut on season bow here after almost a year's absence and has to be respected but there are a few too many questions to answer here (fitnes and the new surface the bigggest) and he's overlooked this time in a very competitive affair. A chance is taken with SILENT FILM to spring a bit of a surprise. Conditions look in his favour and he's dropped back to a threatening mark given he was beaten under two lengths off 98 last July in a hot Sandown handicap. He ran well on Tapeta his only try and he's gone well fresh so in a tight affiar he appeals as a decent each way shot. This year's Lincoln winner Godwinson looks a solid alternative and should go close if taking to the new surface, while Ron O should strip a fair bit fitter this time after his comeback run and is entitled to be in the shake-up along with Mr Professor (winner of last year's Lincoln) who shaped a lot better last time and could be close to finding his best

Previous and Jennys Palace look most interesting of the newcomers

He was poorly drawn at Chester and that effort can be excused, now back over a stiff 5f he can take a step forward and is entitled to go close if getting a handy position early (all below par effort when unable to get a prominent position). Ziggy's Triton is feared off an opening mark of 72 having gone so close last time in a fair novice at Catterick over 5f. He showed enough on his only go on Tapeta when a fair 5th of 10 at Wolverhampton on second start to kick off this season to suggest he can show his best under these conditions. He should go close. selections.comment: BECKFORD'S FOLLY was sent off at a relatively short price for his debut run at Lingfield last time out, and given the fact he came up against some race-fit horses that day, the confidence in the market would suggest people thought he was ready to go in and win on debut. He was a bit too keen throughout the race that day but would have learnt plenty, and given his powerful connections, I can really see him taking a step forward here and winning with the experience under his belt. Romeo Montague only managed 7th on his debut, but was not beaten that far at all, and he can build on that effort here with Ryan Moore booked to ride. Rydale Frosty ran well to a point on debut, and he would have learnt plenty from the experience; he can fill the places here.

selections.comment: Charlie Appleby, William Buick and Godolphin have an excellent record over Newmarket's July track, and they could make it a quickfire double here with HEART OF ETERNITY, who was a very decent 3rd on her debut at Yarmouth last time, only beaten by a length in the end. She was always keeping on that day in the closing stages; therefore, an even further step up in trip might be necessary soon. However, this sort of contest is cherry ripe for her to win now, and she can easily do that with a nice debut effort under her belt. Miss Cartesian has the experience under her belt and is rated 80; therefore, she sets the benchmark; however, this twice-raced filly might just bump into a nice one here. Kohayln hails from a yard that won this race last year, but that horse had some experience under her belt; therefore, I can see their runner this year filling the places.

He landed back-to-back handicaps over this course and distance last season, winning off the marks of 71 and 75; therefore, he is 1 lb below that winning mark and looks primed to go in again here, a venue that he loves so very well. Dashing Dick is another horse who has really good form here, a winner at this venue last season; that was off a 3 lb lower mark, however, and he has gone up 1 lb from his last run, so he might have to settle for another placed finish again. I Maximus has Ryan Moore booked here, and now 2 lbs lower than his last winning mark, he can easily fill the places for an in-form trainer at present.

Short of room with a furlong to go, she soon got to the lead and kept on very well in the closing stages to win by a length, looking like this step up to 6 furlongs will really suit her. She is unbeaten in all three of her starts, and it should be no surprise if she were to make it four in a row here given the form she is in at present. Amberia could not have been any more impressive when winning over 7 furlongs on debut; she has since changed connections and looks to be a really nice prospect for the Dave Loughnane team. Argentine Tango has the experience under her belt, and she was a nice winner last time. However, she might have to settle for a place again here.

selections.comment: TWO TRIBES has the added benefit of Ryan Moore riding him, and the Richard Spencer horse has been in fine form this season without actually winning. A 3rd and two 4th's this season so far in some very decent handicap contests, he could finally get his head in front here for the first time in almost two years. Although he hasn't been winning all that frequently, he has been mixing it up in some pretty hot contests, and with this one being slightly easier than the last few, he can finally get his head in front here. Qazaq has only raced on the all-weather surface; however, he did win on three out of the four occasions he ran and therefore has some talent but might have to settle for 2nd place on his belated turf debut. Hickory was a nice winner of the Victoria Cup on stable debut, and he has since run well but will no doubt have to settle for filling the places here.

selections.comment: ORANGE SKY falls into the "could be anything" category given the fact she is making her handicap debut here today; however, she has shown some good form in novice contests and was an unlucky 3rd last time out when getting a bump with a furlong to go before getting unbalanced and weakening inside the closing furlong. She was sent off as the odds-on favourite that day, so she was expected to win; therefore, it was a disappointing result. However, given the manner of the race, she did well to finish third in the end. She was a very nice winner at Newcastle in September and really looks the sort to build on performances with the more racing she does. The opening mark of 80 could be lenient given her connections and pedigree; therefore, she is worth chancing here. Little Keilee has been running well for James Owen, who does very well with these types, but she will have to settle for 2nd here. As well as Sahana, who has done well to win last time but would need to have really improved to land a contest of this nature; she can run well and place here.

And Daaris does have an 87-day break to overcome here; therefore, he might have to settle with filling the places here.

selections.comment: MISS MAMBO made a solid start when fourth at Chelmsford and looks the one to beat on that form. Calafiori is improving with each run and should be a serious player if continuing on that path, while Miss Apres took a step forward at Goodwood and isn't without a chance back up in trip.

selections.comment: It looks between the two Patrick Neville runners in this six-horse field. MORANDI SECOND looked well back on the flat last time and is taken to edge it over stablemate Cosmic Soul, who has gone close on his last three starts and should be a major threat once more. Rock N Roll Pinkie appeals as the best of the rest and shouldn't be overlooked back at track where she's scored twice over this trip.
